title: Intraday Update: When In Doubt, Run in Place? - Barron's
text:
Brett Arends May 17, 2018 1:11 p.m. ET
Stocks got caught in the middle yet again Thursday morning, as a booming economy faced off against surging bond yields. Illustration: Bloomberg News
The Dow Jones Industrial Average has declined 41.01 points, or 0.2%, to 24,727.92, while the S&P 500 is little changed at 2722.44. The small-cap Russell 2000 index has gained 0.6% to 1626.13. Rising stocks outnumbered falling stocks by about two to one.
The good news and the bad news: We’re partying again like it’s…1973.
The Philadelphia Fed’s latest manufacturing report said new factory orders in the mid-Atlantic region are now rising at their fastest rate since 1973.
The Labor Department came out and said that the number claiming unemployment benefits are also back to 1973 levels.
President Donald trump tweeted that the FBI was spying on his presidential campaign and the scandal is “bigger than Watergate!” Funny, he's not the first person to be talking Watergate lately, either.
One question: Do we all have to go back to wearing bell bottoms and platform soles? Please, please, please no.
Meanwhile, the cost of money is going up and up and up. Ten-year Treasury yields broke above 3.1%, jumping 0.02 percentage point to 3.11% for the first time since 2011.
Oil edged higher too, nearing $72 a barrel, in the wake of the Trump administration’s restoration of sanctions against Iran. European oil giant Total (TOT) has already said it is holding off investing more money in Iran.
Money manager Doug Kass of Seabreeze Capital—the guy who once took on Warren Buffett at the Woodstock of Capitalism —says the stock market’s complacency about all this is worrying . “[M]any of the same investors who were bearish at the February lows are now bullish at the recent mid-May highs,” he writes at realinvestmentadvice.com. “Fear of a large drawdown seems to have been all but eliminated.” His call? We are in a “bull market of complacency…. Consider derisking, now.”
Among the most popular stocks, Apple (AAPL) has declined 0.4%, Facebook (FB) hast icked up 0.1%%, Netflix (NFLX) has dipped 0.1%, Amazon.com (AMZN) has slipped 0.2%, and Alphabet (GOOGL) is little changed. Tesla (TSLA) has fallen just 0.3% after Goldman Sachs said it will need to raise $10 billion in capital over the next two years. Midday Movers
Cenovus Energy (CVE) is up 2.6% to $11.16 after BMO Capital Markets upgraded it to Outperform. Illustration: Bloomberg News
Hasbro (HAS) is up 0.8% to $88.98 after its board authorized a $500 million share-repurchase plan .
Kroger (KR) is up 1.4% to $25.29 on news that it's partnered with online supermarket Ocado Group (OCDGF), which is up 39% to $10.57.
Progressive (PGR) is down 2.2% to $60.28 after KBW downgraded the shares to Market Perform, a day after it reported April results.
World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is up 16.4% to $50.72 on reports that the rights to WWE's Smackdown are available for the right price . Also, Guggenheim reiterated its bullish stance on the stock, writing that the firm's U.S. TV rights renewal "is not only achievable but appears increasingly conservative." — Teresa Rivas
